name: Content Agent — Workflow A (Research & Angle Proposal)

meta.notes: Two independent webhook entry points live on this one canvas, per team preference — not two separate workflow pages. A1 handles Path A search (raw idea, no URL). A2 handles both: Path B (URL provided) scraping straight away, and the continuation after a human has selected sources in Path A. Both triggers converge into the shared scrape -> gate -> angle-proposal -> gate chain. Scraping uses Firecrawl's hosted API, not self-hosted Crawl4AI (see Change entry reversing Decision #2 in week4-progress.md — self-hosting friction on n8n.cloud wasn't worth it). SECRETS: create four n8n Credentials before activating — (1) 'Supabase API' (dedicated credential type — Host = your project URL, Secret Key = your service role key); (2) 'Anthropic' (dedicated credential type — API Key = your Anthropic key); (3) 'Firecrawl' (dedicated credential type — API Key = your Firecrawl key); each used via Authentication -> Predefined Credential Type on their respective nodes. (4) 'Header Auth' named 'Tavily API Key (Authorization header)' (header name 'Authorization', value = 'Bearer <your Tavily key>') — Tavily is the only one with no dedicated n8n credential type. On import n8n will flag each node's credential as unmapped and let you pick the real one you created. Non-secret config (just SUPABASE_URL now) still lives in the 'A1 . Config' / 'A2 . Config' Code nodes.

nodes.name: A1 · Search (Tavily)
nodes.notes: Swap for Serper/Brave/Google CSE if you're using a different search API — same shape (title/url/snippet/date) is all downstream nodes need.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ request_id: $('A1 · Map Results').first().json.requestId, stage: 'research_search', status: 'failed', detail: 'Search returned zero results for the stated idea.' }) }}

nodes.name: A1 · Insert Candidate Sources
nodes.notes: Idempotent on retry: the search stage re-runs the same query and gets the same URLs back, so a plain insert 409s on the sources (request_id, url) unique constraint and crashes the whole workflow - confirmed live, and it left the request stuck at 'researching' with no recoverable path. on_conflict + resolution=ignore-duplicates leaves already-known URLs alone and still inserts genuinely new ones.

nodes.name: A2 · Webhook: Scrape & Propose Angle
nodes.notes: Ping this from Next.js right after intake for Path B (URL), or after the human finishes selecting sources for Path A.

nodes.name: A2 · Auto-select Sources (URL path)
nodes.notes: No-op if this is Path A continuation — those sources were already flipped to 'selected' by the Next.js curation screen, so this filter matches zero rows.

nodes.name: A2 · Fetch Selected Sources
nodes.notes: executeOnce=true: an HTTP Request node runs once per INPUT item by default — with >1 item arriving (e.g. from a loop's 'done' output), it would re-run the identical query that many times, duplicating every row in its array response. Caught live: 2 scraped sources became 4 identical (paired-duplicate) items downstream.

nodes.name: A2 · IF Zero Selected
nodes.notes: Stage 2 hard block: human proceeded having selected zero sources. Should already be blocked client-side, but this is the server-side guard that actually matters.

nodes.notes: Switched from self-hosted Crawl4AI to Firecrawl's hosted API (see Change #5 in week4-progress.md) — no self-hosting/tunnel needed, just an API key.

nodes.name: A2 · IF Zero Scraped
nodes.notes: Stage 2 hard block: every selected source failed to scrape. Stop before spending any AI tokens — do not generate from nothing.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ request_id: $('A2 · Fetch Request Row').first().json.id, stage: 'research_scrape', status: 'failed', detail: 'All selected sources failed to scrape.' }) }}

nodes.name: A2 · IF Resonance/Support Hard Block
nodes.notes: Stage 3 hard blocks: resonance 0-6, or sources genuinely don't support the idea. Either way, no angle gets generated - the human must pick a different idea/angle.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ request_id: $('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.requestId, stage: 'angle_proposal', status: 'failed', detail: $('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.resonance_score <= 6 ? `Audience resonance too low: ${$('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.resonance_score}/15, below the floor of 7. ${$('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.resonance_reasoning}` : `The sources do not support this idea (audience resonance scored ${$('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.resonance_score}/15). ${$('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.resonance_reasoning} Suggested alternative direction: ${$('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.alternative_direction_if_unsupported}` }) }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: 'hard_block', resonance_score: $('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.resonance_score, sources_support_idea: $('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.sources_support_idea, alternative: $('A2 · Parse Claude Response').first().json.alternative_direction_if_unsupported }) }}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify($json.angles.map(a => ({ request_id: $json.requestId, working_title: a.working_title, thesis: a.thesis, section_shape: a.section_shape, resonance_score: $json.resonance_score }))) }}

nodes.notes: Non-secret config only. Supabase, Anthropic, Tavily, and Firecrawl secrets all live in n8n Credentials instead.

nodes.name: A2 · Count Selected Sources
nodes.notes: HTTP Request auto-splits a JSON array response into N items — with zero rows that means zero items, and a downstream IF node never fires on zero input items (neither branch runs, hard block silently skipped). This node always emits exactly one item so the zero-sources hard block actually fires.

nodes.name: A2 · Expand Selected Sources
nodes.notes: Only sources not already 'scraped' get (re)scraped - a retry after partial success shouldn't hit Firecrawl again for sources that already succeeded. Emits an explicit {skip:true} marker (not alwaysOutputData's opaque placeholder) when nothing needs scraping, so the next IF can route around the loop entirely instead of feeding a fake empty source into it.

nodes.name: A2 · Count Scraped Sources
nodes.notes: Same zero-item gap as A2 · Count Selected Sources — a GET returning zero scraped rows produces zero items, which would silently skip the 'all sources failed to scrape' hard block without this wrapper.

nodes.name: A2 · Claude Error: Extract Message
nodes.notes: Claude call failed (rate limit, timeout, bad response, etc). Per the no-partial-progress rule: request status is never advanced this far in the chain, so it's already left exactly where it was before this call — no rollback needed, just a clear log entry and a clean failed response so the human can retry from here.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ request_id: $json.requestId, stage: 'angle_proposal', status: 'failed', detail: `Claude generation failed: ${$json.message}` }) }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: 'claude_failed', detail: $('A2 · Claude Error: Extract Message').first().json.message }) }}
